questions.explanation: Article 109 allows recommendations rather than a veto.

questions.section: Indian Constitution
questions.topic: Union–State Powers and Accountability Institutions
questions.question: Whose records can an eligible RTI request ordinarily seek under the Act?
options: Records held by or accessible to a covered public authority
Unrecorded personal opinions by every elected official
A newly authored opinion that does not exist on file
Any private individual's records regardless of law
questions.explanation: The RTI framework concerns information held by or under the control of public authorities, subject to its terms.

questions.section: Indian Constitution
questions.topic: Decentralisation and Local Self-Government
questions.question: What did the Community Development Programme primarily seek to promote?
options: Development and participation in rural areas
questions.explanation: The programme was an early rural development initiative.

questions.section: Indian Constitution
questions.topic: Decentralisation and Local Self-Government
questions.question: What is the usual constitutional term of a Panchayat, unless sooner dissolved?
questions.explanation: Article 243E provides for five years from the date appointed for its first meeting unless sooner dissolved.

questions.section: Indian Constitution
questions.topic: Legislature, Executive and Judiciary
questions.question: Who appoints the Prime Minister under Article 75?
questions.explanation: The President appoints the Prime Minister under Article 75.

questions.section: Indian Constitution
questions.topic: Constitutional Development, Rights and Basic Structure
questions.question: Which article provides the Supreme Court remedy for enforcement of fundamental rights?
questions.explanation: Article 32 gives the right to move the Supreme Court for enforcement of Part III rights.

questions.section: Indian Constitution
questions.topic: Union–State Powers and Accountability Institutions
questions.question: Which article provides for a possible Inter-State Council?
questions.explanation: Article 263 concerns establishment and duties of an Inter-State Council.

questions.section: Indian Constitution
questions.topic: Federalism, Political Parties, Elections and Defection
questions.question: Which commission chaired by a former Supreme Court judge examined Union–state relations after the Rajamannar Committee and before Punchhi?
questions.explanation: The Sarkaria Commission was appointed in the 1980s to study Union–state relations.

questions.section: Indian Constitution
questions.topic: Constitutional Development, Rights and Basic Structure
questions.question: What does Article 37 state about directive principles?
options: They are enforced only by ordinary civil suits
They supersede every fundamental right without exception
They are not enforceable by any court but fundamental in governance
questions.explanation: Article 37 gives their non-justiciable but fundamental status.

questions.section: Indian Constitution
questions.topic: Union–State Powers and Accountability Institutions
questions.question: Who audits and reports on government accounts subject to the constitutional and statutory framework?
questions.explanation: The CAG undertakes public audit under constitutional and statutory authority.

questions.section: Indian Constitution
questions.topic: Federalism, Political Parties, Elections and Defection
questions.question: Which amendment initially introduced the Tenth Schedule?
questions.explanation: The 52nd Amendment inserted the anti-defection schedule.

questions.section: Indian Constitution
questions.topic: Union–State Powers and Accountability Institutions
questions.question: Which office should ordinarily receive an initial request for information under RTI?
options: Chief Justice of India in all cases
questions.explanation: The Act provides for Public Information Officers to process requests.

questions.section: Indian Constitution
questions.topic: Federalism, Political Parties, Elections and Defection
questions.question: Which constitutional amendment lowered the voting age from twenty-one to eighteen?
questions.explanation: The 61st Amendment lowered the constitutional voting age.

questions.section: Indian Constitution
questions.topic: Constitutional Development, Rights and Basic Structure
questions.question: Which constitutional provision guarantees equality before law and equal protection of laws?
questions.explanation: Article 14 sets out both phrases.

questions.section: Indian Constitution
questions.topic: Federalism, Political Parties, Elections and Defection
questions.question: Which constitutional mechanism primarily addresses failure of constitutional machinery in a state?
questions.explanation: Article 356 provides for a proclamation in the specified circumstances.

questions.section: Indian Constitution
questions.topic: Decentralisation and Local Self-Government
questions.question: What did the Balwant Rai Mehta Committee recommend?
options: A two-tier district–mandal model as its main plan
An entirely centrally appointed village executive
questions.explanation: The committee recommended a three-tier Panchayati Raj framework.

questions.section: Indian Constitution
questions.topic: Constitutional Development, Rights and Basic Structure
questions.question: Which constitutional provision expressly provides free and compulsory education for children aged six to fourteen?
questions.explanation: Article 21A specifies ages six to fourteen.

questions.section: Indian Constitution
questions.topic: Federalism, Political Parties, Elections and Defection
questions.question: Why should a recommendation of a commission be traced to later legal material?
options: A recommendation replaces the need to identify its subject
All commission recommendations become automatic amendments
A recommendation does not itself make a binding constitutional change
Commissions are courts of final appeal
questions.explanation: Implementation requires checking later legal, policy or administrative action.

questions.section: Indian Constitution
questions.topic: Union–State Powers and Accountability Institutions
questions.question: How should a State Lokayukta's exact jurisdiction be checked?
options: Read the applicable state legislation and rules
Assume it equals the Union Lokpal's in every detail
questions.explanation: State arrangements and jurisdiction depend on the relevant legal provisions.

questions.section: Indian Constitution
questions.topic: Decentralisation and Local Self-Government
questions.question: Which amendment gave constitutional status to Panchayats?
questions.explanation: The 73rd Amendment inserted Part IX.

questions.section: Indian Constitution
questions.topic: Constitutional Development, Rights and Basic Structure
questions.question: Which article abolishes untouchability?
questions.explanation: Article 17 abolishes untouchability and provides that enforcing any resulting disability is an offence punishable by law.

questions.section: Indian Constitution
questions.topic: Constitutional Development, Rights and Basic Structure
questions.question: An amendment seeks to remove all constitutional limits on the amending power. Which doctrine is directly relevant?
questions.explanation: Basic structure limits the exercise of the constitutional amendment power.

questions.section: Indian Constitution
questions.topic: Legislature, Executive and Judiciary
questions.question: In the parliamentary system, which actor normally directs day-to-day Union policy through the Cabinet?
options: Prime Minister and the Council of Ministers
questions.explanation: The political executive formulates policy and is responsible to the elected House.

questions.section: Indian Constitution
questions.topic: Federalism, Political Parties, Elections and Defection
questions.question: What is a federal feature of the Constitution?
options: A parliamentary committee appointing all state ministers
All subjects exclusively allocated to one central legislature
A uniform list of every municipal service provider
Constitutional distribution of powers between Union and states
questions.explanation: Division of legislative competence is a federal feature.

questions.section: Indian Constitution
questions.topic: Constitutional Development, Rights and Basic Structure
questions.question: Which amendment inserted the words Socialist and Secular into the Preamble?
questions.explanation: The 42nd Amendment added Socialist and Secular and also modified the reference to the nation's unity.

questions.section: Indian Constitution
questions.topic: Legislature, Executive and Judiciary
questions.question: Who is the constitutional head of a state executive?
questions.explanation: The Constitution vests state executive power in the Governor, within the parliamentary structure.

questions.section: Indian Constitution
questions.topic: Federalism, Political Parties, Elections and Defection
questions.question: Who ordinarily decides a disqualification question under the Tenth Schedule in a House?
options: President of the national party alone
Speaker or Chairman under the applicable procedure
questions.explanation: Paragraph 6 provides decision by the Speaker or Chairman subject to the schedule and judicial review.

questions.section: Indian Constitution
questions.topic: Federalism, Political Parties, Elections and Defection
questions.question: Which commission followed the Sarkaria Commission in a later review of centre–state relations?
questions.explanation: The Punchhi Commission undertook a later review of centre–state relations.

questions.section: Indian Constitution
questions.topic: Constitutional Development, Rights and Basic Structure
questions.question: With which judgment is the basic structure doctrine principally associated?
questions.explanation: Kesavananda Bharati established constitutional limits on the amending power through the basic structure doctrine.

questions.section: Indian Constitution
questions.topic: Decentralisation and Local Self-Government
questions.question: Which body reviews the financial position of Panchayats under Article 243I?
questions.explanation: Article 243I provides for a Finance Commission constituted by the Governor to review Panchayat finances.

questions.section: Indian Constitution
questions.topic: Union–State Powers and Accountability Institutions
questions.question: The National Human Rights Commission takes its statutory basis from which law?
questions.explanation: The NHRC was constituted under the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993.

questions.section: Indian Constitution
questions.topic: Legislature, Executive and Judiciary
questions.question: Who certifies whether a parliamentary bill is a Money Bill under Article 110?
questions.explanation: The Speaker’s decision is specified in Article 110.

questions.section: Indian Constitution
questions.topic: Federalism, Political Parties, Elections and Defection
questions.question: Which schedule contains the Constitution's anti-defection provisions?
questions.explanation: The Tenth Schedule contains the disqualification rules for defection.

questions.section: Indian Constitution
questions.topic: Constitutional Development, Rights and Basic Structure
questions.question: Which law established the broad framework of provincial autonomy before independence?
questions.explanation: The 1935 Act provided for provincial autonomy.

questions.section: Indian Constitution
questions.topic: Legislature, Executive and Judiciary
questions.question: Who can exercise High Court writ jurisdiction under Article 226?
questions.explanation: Article 226 confers writ jurisdiction on High Courts.

questions.section: Indian Constitution
questions.topic: Decentralisation and Local Self-Government
questions.question: What does transfer of functions without funds generally illustrate?
options: A gap between assigned responsibility and operating capacity
An increase in judicial review power
questions.explanation: Local authorities need funding and personnel to carry out responsibilities.

questions.section: Indian Constitution
questions.topic: Union–State Powers and Accountability Institutions
questions.question: Which body performs a statutory anti-corruption ombudsman function for covered Union public functionaries?
questions.explanation: The Lokpal’s jurisdiction and procedure arise from the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act.

questions.section: Indian Constitution
questions.topic: Union–State Powers and Accountability Institutions
questions.question: Which article establishes the GST Council?
questions.explanation: Article 279A concerns the Goods and Services Tax Council.

questions.section: Indian Constitution
questions.topic: Legislature, Executive and Judiciary
questions.question: Article 226 can be used for fundamental rights and which additional purpose?
options: Any other legally cognisable purpose within the provision
questions.explanation: Its text extends to enforcement of rights and for any other purpose.

questions.section: Indian Constitution
questions.topic: Decentralisation and Local Self-Government
questions.question: Which schedule lists matters associated with Municipalities?
questions.explanation: The Twelfth Schedule indicates municipal functions.

questions.section: Indian Constitution
questions.topic: Decentralisation and Local Self-Government
questions.question: What model is most closely associated with the Ashok Mehta Committee?
options: A three-tier model identical to the Balwant Rai Mehta proposal
questions.explanation: The committee proposed a two-tier model centred on district and mandal levels.

questions.section: Indian Constitution
questions.topic: Union–State Powers and Accountability Institutions
questions.question: Which article provides the basic distribution of legislative fields in the Seventh Schedule?
questions.explanation: Article 246 allocates competence across the lists, subject to constitutional provisions.

questions.section: Indian Constitution
questions.topic: Decentralisation and Local Self-Government
questions.question: Which provision concerns Municipalities' reservation of seats?
questions.explanation: Article 243T addresses reservation of seats in Municipalities.

questions.section: Indian Constitution
questions.topic: Legislature, Executive and Judiciary
questions.question: Which provision gives the President ordinance-making power when Parliament is not fully in session and immediate action is considered necessary?
questions.explanation: Article 123 provides the ordinance power under specified conditions.

questions.section: Indian Constitution
questions.topic: Union–State Powers and Accountability Institutions
questions.question: Which schedule contains the Union, State and Concurrent Lists?
questions.explanation: The three legislative lists appear in the Seventh Schedule.

questions.section: Indian Constitution
questions.topic: Decentralisation and Local Self-Government
questions.question: Which amendment added Part IXA on Municipalities?
questions.explanation: The 74th Amendment added Part IXA and the Twelfth Schedule.

questions.section: Indian Constitution
questions.topic: Legislature, Executive and Judiciary
questions.question: What does judicial review assess?
options: Compatibility of challenged action or legislation with controlling law
Which policy is politically most popular
Every department’s expenditure as the statutory auditor
How many legislators should belong to each party by policy preference
questions.explanation: Courts review legality and constitutional validity within their jurisdiction.

questions.section: Indian Constitution
questions.topic: Decentralisation and Local Self-Government
questions.question: What does a District Planning Committee help consolidate?
options: Plans prepared by Panchayats and Municipalities in the district
questions.explanation: Article 243ZD gives district planning committees a plan-consolidation role.

questions.section: Indian Constitution
questions.topic: Federalism, Political Parties, Elections and Defection
questions.question: What is the main difference between party registration and recognition?
options: Every registered party automatically becomes nationally recognised
Registration is determined by the Finance Commission
Recognition by the Lokpal replaces registration
Registration and recognition have separate legal requirements and consequences
questions.explanation: Registration and recognition are governed by different criteria and procedures.

questions.section: Indian Constitution
questions.topic: Legislature, Executive and Judiciary
questions.question: Which institutions constitute Parliament under Article 79?
options: Prime Minister, President and Supreme Court
President, Council of States and House of the People
Council of States and Finance Commission only
House of the People and Council of Ministers only
questions.explanation: Article 79 includes the President and the two Houses.

questions.section: Indian Constitution
questions.topic: Decentralisation and Local Self-Government
questions.question: Which comparison focuses on decentralisation in practice?
options: Legal duties, own revenue, transfers and workforce control
Only the number of Houses at the Union level
Only the number of districts nationwide
Only the existence of a council's printed letterhead
questions.explanation: Actual devolution depends on functions, funds and functionaries.

questions.section: Indian Constitution
questions.topic: Union–State Powers and Accountability Institutions
questions.question: Which article concerns the Comptroller and Auditor General?
questions.explanation: Article 148 establishes the office of CAG.

questions.section: Indian Constitution
questions.topic: Constitutional Development, Rights and Basic Structure
questions.question: Where are the Fundamental Duties listed?
questions.explanation: The duties are in Article 51A in Part IVA.

questions.section: Indian Constitution
questions.topic: Legislature, Executive and Judiciary
questions.question: Which House can a Union Money Bill be introduced in?
options: Either House by the same procedure
questions.explanation: A Money Bill must originate in the House of the People.

questions.section: Indian Constitution
questions.topic: Constitutional Development, Rights and Basic Structure
questions.question: Which part contains the Directive Principles of State Policy?
questions.explanation: Directive Principles appear in Part IV.

title: Mains Paper I · Syllabus sampler
provenance: GateLabs original questions. One question per Annexure II syllabus unit across both sections.

questions.section: Social and Cultural History of Andhra Pradesh
questions.topic: Early Andhra and the Vengi Dynasties
questions.question: An editor cites a Telugu literary work, a royal inscription and a modern textbook to argue that a ruler directly patronised a translation. Which additional finding would most directly support this narrow claim?
options: Evidence that the author and ruler lived a century apart
A later map showing the region in which the language was spoken
A contemporary colophon naming both the translator and the ruler as patron
A census of readers of a modern edition
questions.explanation: A near-contemporary colophon linking the named ruler to the named translator is direct evidence of patronage. A general record of language use cannot establish that link.

questions.section: Social and Cultural History of Andhra Pradesh
questions.topic: Medieval Andhradesa, 11th–16th Centuries
questions.question: A court poem praises a Vijayanagara ruler and prescribes how a king should govern. Which statement gives the best method for using it as evidence of actual administration?
options: Compare its prescriptions with inscriptions or administrative records of how officials acted.
Treat every ideal described by the court poet as an account of implemented policy.
Date every policy from the latest copy of the poem available.
Infer policy from the geographical extent of the poem’s circulation.
questions.explanation: Prescriptive literature can reveal political ideals. Evidence of actual practice needs material that records decisions or administrative actions.

questions.section: Social and Cultural History of Andhra Pradesh
questions.topic: Colonial Rule, Reform and Nationalism in Andhra
questions.question: A 19th-century Andhra reform association prints arguments for widow remarriage and also arranges a marriage. What can these two records establish together that the printed argument alone cannot?
options: The reform became compulsory in every district.
Earlier widow remarriages were legally unknown.
All readers of the printed argument accepted the reform.
The association attempted to put the reform into practice in at least one case.
questions.explanation: Pamphlets show advocacy. A record of an arranged marriage supports implementation in a specific case. Neither establishes province-wide acceptance.

questions.section: Social and Cultural History of Andhra Pradesh
questions.topic: Andhra Movement and the Formation of Andhra State
questions.question: An archive labels a 1954 letter “Andhra Pradesh government, Hyderabad”. Which correction best fits the administrative stage in 1954?
options: Andhra Pradesh was already formed with Hyderabad as capital in 1953.
Andhra State already existed, with Kurnool as its capital. The 1956 Andhra Pradesh merger had not yet taken place.
The 1954 authority still governed the entire former Madras State from Hyderabad.
It was the post-2014 state and Kurnool was chosen as a temporary capital.
questions.explanation: Distinguish the creation of Andhra State in 1953 from the 1956 formation of Andhra Pradesh. The 1954 record belongs between those dates.

questions.section: Social and Cultural History of Andhra Pradesh
questions.topic: Andhra Pradesh Formation and Reorganisation
questions.question: A timeline lists three events: (I) creation of Andhra State, (II) formation of Andhra Pradesh by merging with Telangana, and (III) formation of Telangana as a separate state. Which sequence and interval are both correct?
options: II → I → III; three calendar years between I and II
I → II → III; three calendar years between I and II
I → III → II; eight calendar years between II and III
I → II → III; ten calendar years between I and II
questions.explanation: The events are dated 1953, 1956 and 2014 respectively. The first interval is 1956 − 1953 = 3 calendar years.

questions.section: Indian Constitution
questions.topic: Constitutional Development, Rights and Basic Structure
questions.question: A petitioner relies only on a Directive Principle to demand that a court enforce a specific social policy. Which statement best reflects Article 37?
options: The principle has the same direct enforceability as a Fundamental Right.
The principle is a recommendation to courts only and does not concern lawmaking.
Direct enforceability depends solely on whether both Houses passed a resolution.
The principle guides the State in making laws, while the principle itself cannot be directly enforced by a court.
questions.explanation: Article 37 combines a duty to apply the principles in governance with their non-enforceability by courts.

questions.section: Indian Constitution
questions.topic: Legislature, Executive and Judiciary
questions.question: The Rajya Sabha criticises a Union ministry, while the Lok Sabha continues to support it. Which statement about collective responsibility is most accurate?
options: The Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha. A Rajya Sabha criticism alone does not establish loss of its confidence.
The ministry is collectively responsible to whichever House acts first.
Collective responsibility requires separate confidence votes from both Houses.
The criticism transfers collective responsibility from the Lok Sabha to the Rajya Sabha.
questions.explanation: Article 75(3) places collective responsibility on the Council of Ministers in relation to the House of the People.

questions.section: Indian Constitution
questions.topic: Union–State Powers and Accountability Institutions
questions.question: A report is to recommend both the division of divisible tax proceeds between the Union and States and how the States’ share should be allocated among States. Which institution and distinction are correct?
options: The GST Council; both questions concern the same interstate allocation.
The Comptroller and Auditor General; both decisions follow automatically from auditing state accounts.
The Finance Commission; the first is a Union–State division and the second is an interstate allocation.
A State Finance Commission; it divides Union taxes among all States.
questions.explanation: Article 280 covers both vertical sharing between Union and States and horizontal allocation among States.

questions.section: Indian Constitution
questions.topic: Federalism, Political Parties, Elections and Defection
questions.question: A state MLA is accused of voluntarily giving up party membership. There is a separate dispute over campaign expenditure. Which pairing correctly identifies the framework for the membership issue?
options: The Eleventh Schedule governs disqualification whenever a state election is contested.
The provisions governing money bills determine whether a member defected.
The campaigning dispute must automatically be decided before any defection question can arise.
The Tenth Schedule governs disqualification on defection grounds, distinct from the campaign expenditure issue.
questions.explanation: The Tenth Schedule addresses defection, including voluntarily giving up party membership. Campaign expenditure raises a separate question.

questions.section: Indian Constitution
questions.topic: Decentralisation and Local Self-Government
questions.question: A village project proposes a meeting consisting of all people on the relevant village electoral rolls, followed by work implemented by the elected village body. Which distinction is correct?
options: The meeting is the Gram Sabha and the elected body is the Panchayat.
The meeting is the Panchayat and the elected body is the Gram Sabha.
Both labels denote only the elected members of the village body.
The meeting is the State Finance Commission and the elected body is the Gram Sabha.
questions.explanation: The constitutional definition of Gram Sabha uses electoral registration in the relevant village. The Panchayat is the rural self-government institution.
